anchor_definition: The anchor is the ajax wrapper (_ajax.call) whose body appends the cache-buster `bust` parameter (the current millisecond timestamp) onto every request URL. A degenerate/trivial token: deterministic time, no crypto. Because the timestamp is constructed inline, there is no separate nested 0.7 helper for this case.

primary_anchor.why: Builds settings.url by appending `?bust=`/`&bust=` + (new Date()).getTime(); this is where the observed bust request parameter is generated.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span (file + offsets + sha256 of one complete function).

A returned function name is scored against answer_function ONLY when that identifier is recoverable from the captured slice (named declaration, leading property key, or leading `NAME =`). Anonymous function expressions are graded by span alone.
Explanation must distinguish the anchor from the call-site wrapper, the generic crypto primitive, the sink and same-request decoy fields.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function.

role_oracle.why: Builds settings.url by appending `?bust=`/`&bust=` + (new Date()).getTime(); this is where the observed bust request parameter is generated.
Generic object merge used by _ajax.call to combine defaults with the caller's request options before the bust-bearing URL is assembled. It is on the path but does not generate the bust value.
Builds the /Account/UnitLogin request options and passes them to loginAjax; this is the target login request call-site, but the bust parameter is appended later by _ajax.call.
Thin login request wrapper that calls common.ajax.call(ajax) and updates button state. It forwards the request into the anchor but does not build the bust value.
Collects username/password/code and dispatches the account-login flow into login(); path-critical user trigger, but upstream of bust generation.
Generic network sink reached after _ajax.call has already appended the bust parameter to settings.url. Important on the path, but it emits an already constructed URL.
A URL query-string parser utility; reads URL params but does not generate the bust value. Pure decoy.
A generic deep-clone utility; not on the request-URL bust path.
Uses Date.getTime for date comparison elsewhere in common.js, making it a timestamp-looking decoy. It is not called by the login bust path.

empty_roles.why: No separate complete helper exists: the target timestamp and query parameter are constructed inline inside _ajax.call.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_real_captures; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.anonymous_anchor_name: when answer_function is not recoverable from the captured slice, the name veto is skipped and an exact/unique span match scores the role regardless of submitted name
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The bust timestamp is generated inline inside _ajax.call, so there is no legitimate nested target-specific helper to score at 0.7.
The login page functions identify and dispatch the target /Account/UnitLogin request but do not append bust; they should stay at 0.2.
jQuery.extend is a generic merge utility on the request-preparation path and should not outrank the anchor.
jQuery.ajax emits the already constructed URL and is a sink/wrapper, not the constructor.
Timestamp-looking helpers elsewhere in common.js are off-chain unless they feed settings.url in _ajax.call.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.
audit_notes: Answer match check: 1.json case 12 code and oracle.primary_anchor both resolve to _ajax.call.
Question direction check: the visible question points to the complete function whose body appends `bust`, so it identifies _ajax.call.
